options: A fully managed, serverless Postgres database built into the Databricks platform, with compute and storage separated
A new file format that replaces Delta Lake
A third-party reverse-ETL vendor Databricks integrates with
A caching layer with no persistent storage of its own
questions.explain: Lakebase is a fully managed, serverless, scalable Postgres database built directly into the Databricks Data + AI Platform, for low-latency operational workloads on the same data powering analytics and AI.

questions.q: What manual engineering burden does Lakebase remove, per this lesson?
options: Provisioning a separate OLTP database and hand-building a reverse-ETL pipeline to push curated lakehouse data into it
The need to ever use SQL for querying data
The need for Unity Catalog governance on operational data
The need to ever run a Spark cluster
questions.explain: Before Lakebase, serving curated data to an operational app required provisioning a separate database instance and maintaining a custom reverse-ETL pipeline. Lakebase builds that sync in.

questions.q: What are the two real sync methods from Delta to Lakebase, and their measured latencies?
options: A continuous sync pipeline (~10-15 second lag) and a ForeachWriter real-time mode (~200-300 milliseconds)
Both sync methods have identical sub-millisecond latency
Only one sync method exists: a nightly batch export
Continuous sync (~200-300ms) and ForeachWriter (~10-15 seconds) — the reverse of each option's real numbers
questions.explain: The continuous sync pipeline (managed, configured with a primary key) has 10-15 second lag; the ForeachWriter real-time mode (a direct streaming write) achieves 200-300 millisecond latency at the cost of managing your own streaming query.

questions.q: In the 'Data Diners' end-to-end architecture example, what role does Lakebase play?
options: It receives continuously synced records from the Zerobus-ingested Delta table, and a FastAPI backend reads from it via WebSockets to power a live front-end
It replaces Zerobus as the ingestion mechanism for driver GPS data
It serves as the front-end rendering layer itself, with no backend needed
It is used only for batch reporting once per day
questions.explain: The architecture flows: Zerobus ingests GPS events into Delta, a continuous sync pipeline pushes them into Lakebase, a FastAPI backend streams from Lakebase via WebSockets, and a Databricks Apps front-end visualizes it live.

questions.q: What does 'version control and branch databases like code' mean for Lakebase, per this lesson?
options: Developers can branch a database the way they'd branch a Git repository, useful for testing a schema change against a branch of production data before merging back
Lakebase automatically commits every query to a public GitHub repository
It means Lakebase has no real version-control capability and the phrase is purely marketing
Branching only applies to the Delta tables Lakebase syncs from, never to Lakebase itself
questions.explain: This is a real operational capability: branching a Lakebase database follows the same mental model as a Git feature branch, letting a schema change or migration be tested against a branch before merging to production.
